topic.title: Robust Learning and Adversarial Guarantees
topic.overview: Robust learning limits the damage caused by outliers, malicious perturbations, or corrupted training and inference conditions. The represented papers span robust regression, adversarial classification, randomized smoothing, and dynamical-system identification. Each problem defines a different set of disturbances against which performance is assessed.
topic.whyItMatters: A certificate is meaningful only relative to its perturbation model. Average-case accuracy, worst-case robustness, and probabilistic protection can conflict, so stronger language should not obscure assumptions about attack size, frequency, or distribution.
topic.evolution: Early work replaces Gaussian residual assumptions with heavy-tailed models. Later representatives study adversarial collective classification and multiple perturbation families. Recent theory sharpens nonparametric classification rates and examines sparse attacks on nonlinear systems. The shared development is more explicit control of uncertainty and disturbance structure, not a single defense applicable to every threat.
openQuestions: How can robustness guarantees be matched to realistic deployment disturbances?
When do stronger certificates impose unacceptable losses in ordinary predictive performance?

papers.title: Robust Neural Network Regression for Offline and Online Learning
papers.tldr: Learning a Student-t noise model improves regression robustness and produces stable online learning in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Relaxed Clipping: A Global Training Method for Robust Regression and Classification
papers.tldr: A globally solvable relaxation of loss clipping provides outlier robustness and improves robustness in regression and classification demonstrations.

papers.title: Convex Adversarial Collective Classification
papers.tldr: A convex quadratic program learns collective-classification weights that are optimal against a worst-case adversary with a fixed binary-attribute modification budget.

papers.title: Learning Multiple Models via Regularized Weighting
papers.tldr: Regularizing each model's weights across observations improves robustness, with a provable nonzero breakdown point for clustering under class-balance assumptions.

papers.title: Robust Logistic Regression and Classification
papers.tldr: RoLR uses linear programming to estimate logistic regression parameters with proven robustness to a constant fraction of adversarial outliers.

papers.title: Robust Regression via Hard Thresholding
papers.tldr: TORRENT uses hard thresholding to recover linear models under adversarial response corruption, with conditional guarantees and strong empirical speedups.

papers.title: Blind Attacks on Machine Learners
papers.tldr: Simple data-injection attacks can impose provable learning limits even without access to training data or distribution parameters.

papers.title: Robustness of classifiers: from adversarial to random noise
papers.tldr: Curvature-dependent bounds connect adversarial, semi-random, and random-noise robustness and closely match observations on tested deep classifiers.

papers.title: Bregman Divergence for Stochastic Variance Reduction: Saddle-Point and Adversarial Prediction
papers.tldr: Sufficient statistics and Bregman-based variance reduction accelerate adversarial prediction while preserving a linear convergence guarantee.

papers.title: Formal Guarantees on the Robustness of a Classifier against Adversarial Manipulation
papers.tldr: Instance-specific robustness bounds motivate a regularizer that improves adversarial robustness without accuracy loss in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Adversarial Regression with Multiple Learners
papers.tldr: A game-based approach to adversarial regression with multiple learners produces equilibrium models with improved robustness in experiments.

papers.title: Analyzing the Robustness of Nearest Neighbors to Adversarial Examples
papers.tldr: A theoretical framework explains how nearest-neighbor robustness depends on neighborhood size and motivates a modified robust classifier.

papers.title: Do Outliers Ruin Collaboration?
papers.tldr: The paper establishes a worst-case optimal sample overhead of O(eta n + ln n) for binary learning across partly adversarial sources.

papers.title: Does Distributionally Robust Supervised Learning Give Robust Classifiers?
papers.tldr: The analyzed f-divergence robust classification objective is overly pessimistic, motivating a simpler alternative with empirical support.

papers.title: DRACO: Byzantine-resilient Distributed Training via Redundant Gradients
papers.tldr: DRACO uses redundant gradient computation to remove adversarial updates while reproducing adversary-free training and accelerating reported robust-training comparisons.

papers.title: A Simple Unified Framework for Detecting Out-of-Distribution Samples and Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: A Gaussian model of pretrained network features supplies a Mahalanobis confidence score that detects unfamiliar and adversarial inputs effectively in experiments.

papers.title: A Spectral View of Adversarially Robust Features
papers.tldr: The paper connects robust, varying features to the spectral geometry of data and provides empirical evidence that these features can support robust, accurate models.

papers.title: Adversarial Risk and Robustness: General Definitions and Implications for the Uniform Distribution
papers.tldr: For uniformly distributed binary inputs, the paper clarifies adversarial robustness definitions and proves square-root-dimensional perturbation bounds.

papers.title: Adversarial vulnerability for any classifier
papers.tldr: Under a smooth generative-model assumption, the paper bounds classifier robustness and proves transferable adversarial perturbations exist.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Generalization Requires More Data
papers.tldr: Robust learning can inherently require substantially more data than standard learning, with a similar gap observed in image experiments.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Optimization with Gaussian Processes
papers.tldr: StableOpt optimizes for inputs that retain high performance under adversarial perturbations, with sample guarantees and supporting experiments.

papers.title: Overfitting or perfect fitting? Risk bounds for classification and regression rules that interpolate
papers.tldr: Theory for local interpolating predictors shows that exact training fit can coexist with consistency and, under stated assumptions, optimal statistical rates.

papers.title: PAC-learning in the presence of adversaries
papers.tldr: An adversarial extension of PAC learning characterizes sample-complexity upper bounds through a VC dimension that depends on both classifiers and attacks.

papers.title: Robust Learning of Fixed-Structure Bayesian Networks
papers.tldr: For fully observed discrete Bayesian networks with known structure, the paper gives efficient robust learning with dimension-independent error nearly linear in contamination.

papers.title: Adversarial examples from computational constraints
papers.tldr: Constructed classification tasks show that robust learning can require far more computation than ordinary learning despite needing relatively little data.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: A tight analysis of randomized smoothing turns Gaussian-noise classification performance into scalable certificates of L2 adversarial robustness.

papers.title: Does Data Augmentation Lead to Positive Margin?
papers.tldr: Theoretical analysis shows that common augmentation methods may require exponentially many added examples to enforce a significant classification margin.

papers.title: Generalized No Free Lunch Theorem for Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Under a stated class-conditional distribution assumption, perturbations slightly above the natural noise level can fool any classifier with high probability.

papers.title: Monge blunts Bayes: Hardness Results for Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: A sufficient condition characterizes harmful resource-limited adversaries, connecting Lipschitz classifiers to optimal transport and revealing generalization benefits in toy experiments.

papers.title: On Certifying Non-Uniform Bounds against Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: Feature-specific robustness bounds certify larger regions in experiments and reveal more detailed geometry of neural-network decision boundaries.

papers.title: Rademacher Complexity for Adversarially Robust Generalization
papers.tldr: The analysis reveals dimension dependence in adversarial generalization complexity and suggests one-norm weight constraints as a possible way to improve it.

papers.title: Robust Decision Trees Against Adversarial Examples
papers.tldr: Approximate worst-case split optimization makes adversarially robust training practical for decision trees and boosted tree systems.

papers.title: Robust Learning from Untrusted Sources
papers.tldr: A statistically motivated learning procedure uses multiple data sources while automatically suppressing irrelevant or corrupted information.

papers.title: Sever: A Robust Meta-Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
papers.tldr: Sever strengthens existing learners against structured outliers, with theoretical guarantees and substantial robustness gains on two evaluated datasets.

papers.title: Adversarial Training and Robustness for Multiple Perturbations
papers.tldr: The paper proves a robustness trade-off in a simple setting and shows that defending against multiple perturbation types remains difficult empirically.

papers.title: Empirically Measuring Concentration: Fundamental Limits on Intrinsic Robustness
papers.tldr: A convergent empirical method measures data concentration to investigate distribution-dependent limits on image-classification robustness.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on Adversarial Robustness from Optimal Transport
papers.tldr: Optimal transport characterizes the minimum adversarial classification loss and provides a benchmark for assessing achievable robustness.

papers.title: On Robustness to Adversarial Examples and Polynomial Optimization
papers.tldr: Connecting adversarial robustness to polynomial optimization yields provable learning algorithms and principled certification and attack methods for specified model classes.

papers.title: On the Hardness of Robust Classification
papers.tldr: Robust learning faces strong sample and computational barriers, with feasibility depending on distributional assumptions and the adversary's perturbation budget.

papers.title: Provably robust boosted decision stumps and trees against adversarial attacks
papers.tldr: Efficient exact robustness calculations for boosted stumps and robust-loss bounds for boosted trees enable provably robust boosting methods.

papers.title: Provably Robust Deep Learning via Adversarially Trained Smoothed Classifiers
papers.tldr: Adversarial training with an attack tailored to smoothed classifiers improves their provable l2 robustness on ImageNet and CIFAR-10.

papers.title: Reverse KL-Divergence Training of Prior Networks: Improved Uncertainty and Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Reverse-KL training improves Prior Networks and increases the effort needed for evaluated adaptive attacks.

papers.title: Robustness to Adversarial Perturbations in Learning from Incomplete Data
papers.tldr: A unified robust semi-supervised framework quantifies the role of unlabeled data and supports a convergent, empirically competitive algorithm.

papers.title: Theoretical Analysis of Adversarial Learning: A Minimax Approach
papers.tldr: A minimax reformulation yields adversarial risk bounds with data-dependent terms that can guide robustness optimization.

papers.title: Theoretical evidence for adversarial robustness through randomization
papers.tldr: The paper relates inference-time randomization to adversarial robustness and derives a new upper bound on randomized networks' adversarial risk gap.

papers.title: Tight Certificates of Adversarial Robustness for Randomly Smoothed Classifiers
papers.tldr: The paper broadens randomized-smoothing robustness certificates to discrete perturbations and shows how classifier structure can tighten guarantees.

papers.title: Adversarial Risk via Optimal Transport and Optimal Couplings
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal binary adversarial risk using optimal transport and derives optimal robust classifiers for several one-dimensional distributions.

papers.title: Black-box Certification and Learning under Adversarial Perturbations
papers.tldr: The paper analyzes when robust learning and black-box certification are possible, and connects efficient adversarial attacks to sample-efficient robust learning.

papers.title: Certified Robustness to Label-Flipping Attacks via Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: A smoothing framework provides deterministic, per-prediction certificates that linear classifiers withstand a bounded number of adversarial training-label changes.

papers.title: Curse of Dimensionality on Randomized Smoothing for Certifiable Robustness
papers.tldr: For broad smoothing families, certifiable robustness under lp perturbations with p greater than 2 deteriorates with dimension and cannot improve on Gaussian dimension scaling.

papers.title: Efficiently Learning Adversarially Robust Halfspaces with Noise
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes efficient robust learning of halfspaces in the realizable setting and gives an efficient algorithm for ℓp perturbations with random label noise.

papers.title: High-dimensional Robust Mean Estimation via Gradient Descent
papers.tldr: A structural result makes gradient descent sufficient to obtain near-optimal robust mean estimates from a natural nonconvex formulation.

papers.title: Interpreting Robust Optimization via Adversarial Influence Functions
papers.tldr: Adversarial Influence Functions efficiently characterize how robust optimization changes model solutions and prediction losses on natural data.

papers.title: Learning Adversarially Robust Representations via Worst-Case Mutual Information Maximization
papers.tldr: Maximizing worst-case mutual information provides an unsupervised training principle for representations with empirically supported adversarial robustness.

papers.title: On the Sample Complexity of Adversarial Multi-Source PAC Learning
papers.tldr: Finite-sample guarantees show that learning from multiple sources can remain viable and beneficial despite adversarial corruption of some sources.

papers.title: Optimal Robust Learning of Discrete Distributions from Batches
papers.tldr: The paper gives a polynomial-time estimator for corrupted batches that uses an optimal number of batches and achieves essentially optimal accuracy.

papers.title: Randomized Smoothing of All Shapes and Sizes
papers.tldr: A general theory of randomized smoothing improves l1 robustness certificates and establishes high-dimensional limits for methods using only perturbed-label statistics.

papers.title: Sharp Statistical Guaratees for Adversarially Robust Gaussian Classification
papers.tldr: For Gaussian-mixture classification, the paper matches optimal robust excess-risk bounds with an efficient estimator using adversarial signal-to-noise ratio.

papers.title: When are Non-Parametric Methods Robust?
papers.tldr: Nearest-neighbor and kernel classifiers are asymptotically robust under separation conditions, and Adversarial Pruning extends the guarantee to general distributions.

papers.title: A Game Theoretic Analysis of Additive Adversarial Attacks and Defenses
papers.tldr: Under a locally linear binary-classifier model, Fast Gradient Method and Randomized Smoothing form a Nash equilibrium with a finite-sample defense approximation.

papers.title: A General Method for Robust Learning from Batches
papers.tldr: A general framework yields robust distribution estimation and classification algorithms when some data batches are corrupted or adversarial.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness of Supervised Sparse Coding
papers.tldr: The paper derives robust-risk bounds and classification certificates for sparse learned representations coupled with linear classifiers.

papers.title: Adversarial robustness via robust low rank representations
papers.tldr: Natural low-rank representations strengthen adversarial robustness certificates, supported by a new algorithm for bounding how representations transform perturbations.

papers.title: Black-Box Certification with Randomized Smoothing: A Functional Optimization Based Framework
papers.tldr: A functional optimization framework designs non-Gaussian smoothing distributions for stronger certification across several adversarial perturbation measures.

papers.title: Certifiably Adversarially Robust Detection of Out-of-Distribution Data
papers.tldr: Training on certified confidence bounds enables robust out-of-distribution detection with little reported loss in classification accuracy.

papers.title: Consistency Regularization for Certified Robustness of Smoothed Classifiers
papers.tldr: Encouraging consistent predictions under Gaussian noise improves the certified robustness of smoothed classifiers with comparatively low training cost.

papers.title: (De)Randomized Smoothing for Certifiable Defense against Patch Attacks
papers.tldr: A deterministic smoothing defense exploits patch geometry to improve certified robustness and scale certification to ImageNet.

papers.title: Detection as Regression: Certified Object Detection with Median Smoothing
papers.tldr: Reducing detection to regression and using median smoothing yields a training-free certified defense against l_2-bounded attacks.

papers.title: Distributional Robustness with IPMs and links to Regularization and GANs
papers.tldr: The paper links robustness under integral probability metrics to regularization penalties and extends that analysis to GAN objectives and discriminator choices.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Local Non-parametric Conditional Estimation
papers.tldr: A worst-case distributional objective produces robust local estimates and admits efficient convex solutions in broadly applicable settings.

papers.title: Fast Adversarial Robustness Certification of Nearest Prototype Classifiers for Arbitrary Seminorms
papers.tldr: For nearest-prototype classifiers using seminorm-based dissimilarities, the hypothesis margin provides a tight, constant-time robustness certificate.

papers.title: Higher-Order Certification For Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: Richer information about smoothed classifiers enlarges certified safety regions without changing the smoothing scheme.

papers.title: Lipschitz Bounds and Provably Robust Training by Laplacian Smoothing
papers.tldr: Graph-based constrained training achieves provable robustness bounds and characterizes the sensitivity that must remain at a desired performance level.

papers.title: Online Robust Regression via SGD on the l1 loss
papers.tldr: Under an obliviously corrupted Gaussian linear model, averaged SGD on absolute error consistently estimates the true parameter with a rate independent of corruption magnitude.

papers.title: Provably Robust Metric Learning
papers.tldr: A certifiably robust metric-learning algorithm improves adversarial performance without sacrificing clean performance in the reported comparisons.

papers.title: Reducing Adversarially Robust Learning to Non-Robust PAC Learning
papers.tldr: Robust learning can be reduced to black-box ordinary PAC learning with an unavoidable logarithmic dependence on the number of allowed perturbations.

papers.title: The Generalized Lasso with Nonlinear Observations and Generative Priors
papers.tldr: Generalized Lasso recovers signals described by Lipschitz generators from nonlinear measurements, with conditional sample and robustness guarantees.

papers.title: Evaluating Robustness of Predictive Uncertainty Estimation: Are Dirichlet-based Models Reliable?
papers.tldr: Adversarial evaluations expose weaknesses in Dirichlet-based uncertainty estimates, while a median-smoothing approach substantially improves their robustness.

papers.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Distributionally Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: The paper derives optimal ordinary-risk versus adversarial-risk tradeoffs for three model settings in an infinite-data regime.

papers.title: Generalised Lipschitz Regularisation Equals Distributional Robustness
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when transportation-based distributional robustness equals Lipschitz regularization and tightly bounds the gap under mild assumptions.

papers.title: Improved, Deterministic Smoothing for L_1 Certified Robustness
papers.tldr: DSSN uses input-space splitting to deliver efficient deterministic L1 robustness certificates for quantized data, with improved reported certificate sizes.

papers.title: PAC-Learning for Strategic Classification
papers.tldr: Strategic VC-dimension unifies learnability analysis for manipulated inputs and enables statistical and computational characterizations of strategic linear classification.

papers.title: Provable Robustness of Adversarial Training for Learning Halfspaces with Noise
papers.tldr: Under anti-concentration assumptions, adversarial training learns noise-tolerant robust halfspaces, with stronger error guarantees from a sigmoidal loss.

papers.title: Query Complexity of Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: A decision-boundary entropy bound links the queries needed for strong adversarial attacks to provable security in two synthetic learning settings.

papers.title: Robust Density Estimation from Batches: The Best Things in Life are (Nearly) Free
papers.tldr: For the studied distribution family, robust learning from corrupted batches matches clean-data sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Sample Complexity of Robust Linear Classification on Separated Data
papers.tldr: Separated classes can still make robust learning sample-intensive, while sufficiently large separation relative to perturbations permits faster rates.

papers.title: A PAC-Bayes Analysis of Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: The paper develops PAC-Bayesian bounds on perturbation-averaged adversarial risk for majority-vote predictors that can also guide training.

papers.title: A Universal Law of Robustness via Isoperimetry
papers.tldr: Under stated distributional and parameterization assumptions, smoothly fitting data requires a dimension-dependent increase in model size.

papers.title: Adversarial Regression with Doubly Non-negative Weighting Matrices
papers.tldr: A matrix-based formulation makes adversarial sample reweighting for kernel regression efficiently solvable under two specified uncertainty measures.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness of Streaming Algorithms through Importance Sampling
papers.tldr: Importance sampling and merge-and-reduce provide adversarial robustness for a broad range of streaming learning algorithms.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness with Semi-Infinite Constrained Learning
papers.tldr: A distribution-based formulation of adversarial training motivates a sampling method that can improve the trade-off between ordinary accuracy and robustness.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Change Point Detection
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes how adversarial contamination limits mean-change detection and develops a method with conditionally near-optimal localization accuracy.

papers.title: Adversarially robust learning for security-constrained optimal power flow
papers.tldr: The paper combines adversarial optimization and implicit differentiation to schedule power generation against simultaneous equipment outages.

papers.title: Calibration and Consistency of Adversarial Surrogate Losses
papers.tldr: The paper distinguishes adversarial surrogate calibration from consistency and identifies both impossibility results and conditions that permit consistency.

papers.title: Center Smoothing: Certified Robustness for Networks with Structured Outputs
papers.tldr: Center smoothing certifies bounded changes in structured outputs under norm-bounded adversarial changes to the input.

papers.title: Consistent Non-Parametric Methods for Maximizing Robustness
papers.tldr: The paper defines an accuracy-preserving target for adaptive robustness and gives sufficient conditions for non-parametric classifiers to approach it.

papers.title: Corruption Robust Active Learning
papers.tldr: A streaming active-learning algorithm preserves optimal label efficiency without corruption and bounds the additional cost and error caused by adversarial labels.

papers.title: Exponential Separation between Two Learning Models and Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: A theoretical separation shows that interactive counterexamples can dramatically reduce sample needs and yield robustness under an equivalence-query adversary.

papers.title: Fair Classification with Adversarial Perturbations
papers.tldr: A classification framework provides nearly tight accuracy and fairness guarantees when an adversary corrupts protected attributes.

papers.title: Improving Robustness using Generated Data
papers.tldr: Synthetic data generated from the original training set can substantially improve adversarial robustness, with benefits even from Gaussian random examples in the studied settings.

papers.title: On the Algorithmic Stability of Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: The paper links weaker stability in adversarial training to nondifferentiability and analyzes noise injection as a remedy.

papers.title: On the Existence of The Adversarial Bayes Classifier
papers.tldr: The paper gives sufficient conditions for an adversarial Bayes-optimal classifier to exist, supporting possible future analysis of surrogate-loss consistency.

papers.title: Probabilistic Margins for Instance Reweighting in Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: Continuous, path-independent probability margins improve how adversarial training identifies and emphasizes vulnerable examples.

papers.title: Relaxing Local Robustness
papers.tldr: Two relaxed robustness properties allow task-appropriate relationships among labels while supporting efficient certification and improved reported certified accuracy.

papers.title: ReLU Regression with Massart Noise
papers.tldr: An efficient ReLU regression algorithm exactly recovers parameters under Massart noise and mild anti-concentration assumptions.

papers.title: Robust and Fully-Dynamic Coreset for Continuous-and-Bounded Learning (With Outliers) Problems
papers.tldr: The paper constructs outlier-robust coresets that support dynamic updates and can have size governed by the parameter space's doubling dimension.

papers.title: Robustness between the worst and average case
papers.tldr: The paper measures robustness between random and worst-case perturbations and estimates these intermediate metrics efficiently using MCMC.

papers.title: SmoothMix: Training Confidence-calibrated Smoothed Classifiers for Certified Robustness
papers.tldr: SmoothMix trains on mixtures along adversarial directions to calibrate smoothed classifiers and improve certified ℓ2 robustness.

papers.title: The Many Faces of Adversarial Risk
papers.tldr: The paper rigorously relates definitions of adversarial risk to optimal transport, robust hypothesis testing, and game-theoretic equilibrium.

papers.title: Towards Better Understanding of Training Certifiably Robust Models against Adversarial Examples
papers.tldr: Certifiable robustness training depends on both bound tightness and loss-landscape smoothness, motivating a method that combines the two.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness against Multiple and Single $l_p$-Threat Models via Quick Fine-Tuning of Robust Classifiers
papers.tldr: Short fine-tuning with Extreme norm Adversarial Training extends existing classifiers’ robustness across multiple perturbation norms.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness Under the Bounded Support Set
papers.tldr: Distance-based certification frameworks analyze bounded-support smoothing and establish negative robustness properties for the uniform distributions studied.

papers.title: Double Sampling Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: DSRS tightens randomized-smoothing robustness certificates using an additional noise distribution, with conditional theory and experiments supporting larger certified radii.

papers.title: Fast Provably Robust Decision Trees and Boosting
papers.tldr: FPRDT and PRAdaBoost combine provable adversarial robustness with efficient tree training and strong comparative experimental performance.

papers.title: Intriguing Properties of Input-Dependent Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: Input-dependent smoothing faces dimensionality-driven restrictions, but a carefully constrained framework can support valid robustness guarantees.

papers.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Causal Algorithmic Recourse
papers.tldr: The paper develops recourse methods robust to feature uncertainty and shows how classifier design can help such recommendations exist.

papers.title: On the Generalization Analysis of Adversarial Learning
papers.tldr: The paper bounds adversarial generalization using training risk, model complexity, and allowed perturbations, with fast-rate results for smooth losses.

papers.title: On the Robustness of CountSketch to Adaptive Inputs
papers.tldr: A tailored CountSketch estimator supports quadratically many adaptive queries in sketch size, improving on prior generic robustness approaches.

papers.title: Probabilistically Robust Learning: Balancing Average and Worst-case Performance
papers.tldr: Probabilistic robustness targets most perturbations, balancing ordinary accuracy and robustness with lower training cost than adversarial training.

papers.title: Provably Adversarially Robust Nearest Prototype Classifiers
papers.tldr: New exact computations and lower bounds strengthen robustness certification and training for interpretable nearest-prototype classifiers.

papers.title: RetrievalGuard: Provably Robust 1-Nearest Neighbor Image Retrieval
papers.tldr: RetrievalGuard smooths an image retrieval model to certify Recall@1 robustness against adversarial perturbations within a calculable ℓ₂ radius.

papers.title: Robust Kernel Density Estimation with Median-of-Means principle
papers.tldr: MoM-KDE combines kernel density estimation with median-of-means robustness, providing finite-sample guarantees and competitive results at lower computational complexity.

papers.title: A Characterization of Semi-Supervised Adversarially Robust PAC Learnability
papers.tldr: With enough unlabeled data, adversarially robust learning can require arbitrarily fewer labels, with nearly matching theoretical bounds.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Learning: A Generic Minimax Optimal Learner and Characterization
papers.tldr: A global graph construction enables minimax-optimal adversarially robust learning and a dimension characterizing robust learnability and sample complexity.

papers.title: Boosting Barely Robust Learners: A New Perspective on Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Barely robust learners can be boosted to strong robustness under a larger-perturbation-set requirement that the paper shows is necessary.

papers.title: Double Bubble, Toil and Trouble: Enhancing Certified Robustness through Transitivity
papers.tldr: Combining nearby certificates through geometry and transitivity improves randomized-smoothing robustness guarantees beyond single-input score information.

papers.title: MultiGuard: Provably Robust Multi-label Classification against Adversarial Examples
papers.tldr: MultiGuard certifies that a certain number of true labels survive adversarial perturbations with bounded l2 norm.

papers.title: On Optimal Learning Under Targeted Data Poisoning
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes optimal realizable learning error under targeted poisoning and proves an unavoidable multiplicative penalty for deterministic agnostic learners.

papers.title: On Robust Multiclass Learnability
papers.tldr: Adversarial graph and Natarajan dimensions provide upper and lower sample-complexity bounds for robust multiclass learning.

papers.title: On the Tradeoff Between Robustness and Fairness
papers.tldr: Stronger adversarial training can widen class-wise robustness disparities, and the proposed FAT method mitigates this empirically observed tradeoff.

papers.title: Robust Bayesian Regression via Hard Thresholding
papers.tldr: Combining prior information, hard thresholding, and Bayesian reweighting improves regression robustness against the adaptive corruption studied in the paper.

papers.title: Smoothed Embeddings for Certified Few-Shot Learning
papers.tldr: The paper extends randomized smoothing to normalized embeddings and derives l2 robustness certificates relevant to prototype-based few-shot learning.

papers.title: Towards Consistency in Adversarial Classification
papers.tldr: The paper shows why convex surrogate losses fail adversarial calibration and consistency, and derives conditions to guide alternative losses.

papers.title: Trimmed Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Robust Generalized Linear Model
papers.tldr: Iterative trimmed maximum likelihood achieves near-optimal risk under label corruption and extends robustly to corrupted inputs and labels.

papers.title: When are Local Queries Useful for Robust Learning?
papers.tldr: Local equivalence queries enable distribution-free robust ERM when their radius matches the adversary's budget, while smaller radii leave broad impossibility results.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust PAC Learnability of Real-Valued Functions
papers.tldr: Finite fat-shattering dimension suffices for adversarially robust regression learning, although some non-convex classes require learners to output functions outside the class.

papers.title: Beyond the Universal Law of Robustness: Sharper Laws for Random Features and Neural Tangent Kernels
papers.tldr: In the settings studied, extra parameters cannot make random features robust, whereas neural tangent kernels with even activations achieve the universal robustness bound.

papers.title: Computational Asymmetries in Robust Classification
papers.tldr: The paper proves computational asymmetries between attack and defense and introduces an inference-time certification approach that reverses their direction.

papers.title: Dimension-independent Certified Neural Network Watermarks via Mollifier Smoothing
papers.tldr: Mollifier smoothing provides dimension-independent watermark certificates across lp attack norms, with a PDE-based approximation to reduce computational difficulty.

papers.title: Improving l1-Certified Robustness via Randomized Smoothing by Leveraging Box Constraints
papers.tldr: Using valid image-value bounds strengthens randomized-smoothing l1 robustness certificates without changing classifiers or smoothing distributions.

papers.title: On the Robustness of Randomized Ensembles to Adversarial Perturbations
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes randomized ensembles’ robustness limits and introduces BARRE, a training method effective against tested infinity-norm-bounded attacks.

papers.title: Understanding the Impact of Adversarial Robustness on Accuracy Disparity
papers.tldr: The paper separates robustness-induced accuracy loss from class-imbalance effects and shows that distribution tails change how imbalance affects accuracy disparity.

papers.title: Adaptive Data Analysis in a Balanced Adversarial Model

papers.title: Adversarial Examples Might be Avoidable: The Role of Data Concentration in Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: The paper shows how data concentration can determine whether robust classifiers exist and enable stronger certification in certain structured settings.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Learning with Uncertain Perturbation Sets
papers.tldr: Partial knowledge of possible adversarial perturbations and the option to abstain enable robust learnability results under the paper's stated information assumptions.

papers.title: Asymmetric Certified Robustness via Feature-Convex Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Feature-convex networks provide efficiently computable robustness certificates for a sensitive class in asymmetric binary classification.

papers.title: Characterizing the Optimal $0-1$ Loss for Multi-class Classification with a Test-time Attacker
papers.tldr: A conflict-hypergraph framework characterizes optimal adversarial classification loss and helps measure how far trained multi-class classifiers fall short.

papers.title: Distribution Learnability and Robustness
papers.tldr: Distribution learnability implies robustness to additive contamination, but this implication fails in general for subtractive contamination.

papers.title: Efficient Testable Learning of Halfspaces with Adversarial Label Noise
papers.tldr: A polynomial-time tester-learner provides conditional error guarantees for halfspaces with adversarial label noise and supports label-efficient active learning.

papers.title: On Proper Learnability between Average- and Worst-case Robustness
papers.tldr: Some relaxations of worst-case robust loss restore proper PAC learnability for VC classes, while another natural relaxation does not.

papers.title: On the Role of Randomization in Adversarially Robust Classification
papers.tldr: Randomization can beat a fixed base family under stated conditions, yet every probabilistic binary classifier has a better deterministic counterpart.

papers.title: Provable Adversarial Robustness for Group Equivariant Tasks: Graphs, Point Clouds, Molecules, and More
papers.tldr: The paper defines robustness that respects task symmetries and develops certification methods for equivariant models and graph tasks.

papers.title: Reliable learning in challenging environments
papers.tldr: The paper develops a reliable learner with provably optimal guarantees for studied adversarial attacks and natural distribution shifts.

papers.title: Revisiting Adversarial Robustness Distillation from the Perspective of Robust Fairness
papers.tldr: Fair-ARD emphasizes difficult classes during robustness distillation, improving worst-class protection and slightly improving overall robustness in experiments.

papers.title: Robust Distributed Learning: Tight Error Bounds and Breakdown Point under Data Heterogeneity
papers.tldr: A broader heterogeneity model yields tight distributed-learning error bounds and an adversarial breakdown threshold below one half.

papers.title: RS-Del: Edit Distance Robustness Certificates for Sequence Classifiers via Randomized Deletion
papers.tldr: RS-Del uses random deletions to certify sequence classifiers against bounded insertion, deletion, and substitution attacks.

papers.title: The Adversarial Consistency of Surrogate Risks for Binary Classification
papers.tldr: The paper completely characterizes distribution-independent adversarially consistent surrogate losses and shows they are more restricted than ordinary consistent losses.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Hypothesis Transfer Learning
papers.tldr: Robust transfer learning can achieve faster generalization rates when auxiliary hypotheses provide a sufficiently good adversarially robust initialization.

papers.title: Consistent Adversarially Robust Linear Classification: Non-Parametric Setting
papers.tldr: A progressively smoothed estimator achieves consistent adversarially robust linear classification under mild distributional conditions, with an optimal rate available at an optimization cost.

papers.title: Delving into the Convergence of Generalized Smooth Minimax Optimization
papers.tldr: The paper proves convergence for variants of basic minimax algorithms under generalized smoothness, beyond the usual Lipschitz-smooth setting.

papers.title: Fast White-Box Adversarial Streaming Without a Random Oracle
papers.tldr: Under a subexponential Learning with Errors security assumption, the paper gives fast, near-optimal sparse recovery against white-box streaming adversaries without a random oracle.

papers.title: Multigroup Robustness
papers.tldr: Multigroup robustness gives each overlapping subpopulation guarantees that degrade only with the corruption within that group.

papers.title: Precise Accuracy / Robustness Tradeoffs in Regression: Case of General Norms
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes achievable robustness in linear regression and separates regimes with no accuracy cost from those where a tradeoff may be unavoidable.

papers.title: Robust Learning-Augmented Dictionaries
papers.tldr: RobustSL exploits accurate access-frequency predictions while guaranteeing logarithmic operation time even under adversarial predictions.

papers.title: Achievable distributional robustness when the robust risk is only partially identified
papers.tldr: The paper defines achievable robustness when training environments reveal only part of the worst-case risk and shows why existing methods can fall short.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Dense-Sparse Tradeoffs via Heavy-Hitters
papers.tldr: Improved heavy-hitter detection and tail estimation yield better memory tradeoffs for adversarially robust Lp estimation in turnstile streams.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized $\alpha$-Smoothing for Regression Models
papers.tldr: Alpha-trimmed randomized smoothing extends robustness certification to regression with a tunable robustness–utility trade-off.

papers.title: Diffusion Models are Certifiably Robust Classifiers
papers.tldr: The paper proves robustness guarantees for diffusion classifiers and tightens certification through classifiers designed for Gaussian-corrupted inputs.

papers.title: High-dimensional (Group) Adversarial Training in Linear Regression
papers.tldr: Under stated structural conditions, adversarial training achieves near-minimax regression error, with sharper bounds for certain group-sparse settings.

papers.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Benjamini Hochberg
papers.tldr: Under identified conditions, even one adversarial test-score change can substantially undermine Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery control.

papers.title: Tolerant Algorithms for Learning with Arbitrary Covariate Shift
papers.tldr: Improved outlier-removal analysis yields efficient and more shift-tolerant learning algorithms in frameworks that permit abstention.

papers.title: Treatment of Statistical Estimation Problems in Randomized Smoothing for Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Confidence-sequence estimators reduce randomized-smoothing certification work with optimal sample complexity, while randomized confidence intervals strengthen certificates.

papers.title: Verifiably Robust Conformal Prediction
papers.tldr: VRCP uses neural network verification to provide adversarially robust conformal prediction for classification and regression under arbitrary norm-bounded perturbations.

papers.title: Average Certified Radius is a Poor Metric for Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: Average certified radius can reward gains on easy examples while concealing weaker robustness on hard examples.

papers.title: Certifiably Robust Model Evaluation in Federated Learning under Meta-Distributional Shifts
papers.tldr: The paper certifies federated model performance on unseen client networks under an explicitly bounded shift in client distributions.

papers.title: Gradient Flow Provably Learns Robust Classifiers for Orthonormal GMMs
papers.tldr: For orthonormal Gaussian mixtures, gradient flow on a specified two-layer network provably learns optimal robustness without adversarial examples.

papers.title: Optimal Fair Learning Robust to Adversarial Distribution Shift
papers.tldr: Randomization restores accuracy robustness for fair Bayes optimal classifiers under adversarial distribution noise, while requiring randomness at at most one data point.

papers.title: Position: Certified Robustness Does Not (Yet) Imply Model Security
papers.tldr: The paper argues that certified robustness still faces practical and interpretive gaps before it can support real-world model security.

papers.title: Probably Approximately Global Robustness Certification
papers.tldr: Sampling combined with local robustness checks yields formal probabilistic global guarantees with sample requirements independent of input dimension and class count.

papers.title: Provably Cost-Sensitive Adversarial Defense via Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: This method adapts randomized smoothing to certify and train adversarial robustness according to the unequal costs of different mistakes.

papers.title: Quadratic Upper Bound for Boosting Robustness
papers.tldr: A quadratic upper-bound loss improves existing fast adversarial training methods, with evidence suggesting smoother loss landscapes help explain the gains.

papers.title: Sample-specific Noise Injection for Diffusion-based Adversarial Purification
papers.tldr: SSNI adapts diffusion-purification noise to each input using score norms, improving reported accuracy and robustness.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness of Nonparametric Regression
papers.tldr: Properly regularized smoothing splines tolerate a vanishing fraction of arbitrarily corrupted samples, reaching the fundamental corruption threshold for consistent estimation.

papers.title: MIBP-Cert: Certified Training against Data Perturbations with Mixed-Integer Bilinear Programs
papers.tldr: MIBP-Cert soundly bounds models reachable under specified training-data perturbations using mixed-integer bilinear optimization and tractable relaxations.

papers.title: On the Optimality of the Median-of-Means Estimator under Adversarial Contamination
papers.tldr: Median-of-means is minimax optimal under adversarial contamination for specified moment classes, but suboptimal for light-tailed distributions.

papers.title: Robust Satisficing Gaussian Process Bandits Under Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: Two Gaussian-process algorithms target reliable threshold attainment under adversarial perturbations, with guarantees that depend on different assumptions about the adversary.

papers.title: Higher-Order Certified Robustness for Regression
papers.tldr: The paper uses local prediction geometry to certify smoothed regression models, obtaining tighter certificates with gradients on MNIST rotation.

papers.title: On the Sharp Input-Output Analysis of Nonlinear Systems under Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: The paper proves matching estimation-error bounds for nonlinear input-output learning when informed adversarial attacks occur sufficiently infrequently.

papers.title: Probabilistic Robustness Certificates against Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: Barrier certificates provide probabilistic adversarial-robustness guarantees that explicitly account for stochastic training and bounded worst-case perturbations.

papers.title: Tight Stability Bounds for Robust Distributed Learning: Byzantine Failures Hurt Generalization More than Data Poisoning
papers.tldr: Tight stability bounds show that Byzantine communication failures permit worse generalization guarantees than corruption confined to workers' training data.
